title: A research plan on artificial intelligence in courts

lines.t: Come in, Samira. I have read your draft proposal on artificial intelligence in courts, and I would like to go through it section by section.
Thank you. I was a little worried that the scope is too wide, to be honest.
It is, but not in the way you think. You say you will study risk assessment tools, translation software and case allocation systems. That is three projects, not one.
I included all three because each affects how fair a trial feels to ordinary people.
I understand, but a doctoral committee wants depth. I suggest you keep risk assessment tools and drop the other two, at least for the main study.
Could I mention translation software as a future direction in the conclusion?
Certainly, a short paragraph would be fine. Now, your methods. You plan to interview forty judges. How did you arrive at that number?
Mostly from similar studies. But I realise judges are very busy, so I might only reach fifteen.
Fifteen is realistic, and it is enough if you combine it with court observation. Have you thought about ethics approval?
I have started the form. The difficulty is that some courts will not allow recordings, so I would rely on handwritten notes.
Then please say so clearly. Reviewers dislike surprises, and handwritten notes affect how you can quote people.
I will add a section on that. I also wanted to ask about the data. A vendor has offered me access to its risk scores for one region.
That is interesting, but be careful. If the company controls what you see, your independence could be questioned.
Ask for a written agreement that gives you the right to publish whatever you find.
Even if the findings are critical of the product?
Especially then. Without that clause, I would not sign anything.
Understood. My other worry is the timeline. I have given myself six months for fieldwork.
That is too optimistic. Gaining access to courts takes time, so plan for nine months, and begin the first contacts while you are still writing the proposal.
That would push the writing stage into the third year.
It would, but a third year for writing is normal. What matters is that the first chapter is nearly finished by the end of year one.
I could draft the literature review during the access negotiations.
Exactly. And on that note, your reading list is strong on law, but I see almost nothing from computer science.
I was afraid I would not understand it.
You do not need to follow the mathematics. You need to know how these tools are trained and tested, because your argument depends on that.
I will send you two accessible articles.
That would be a great help. Should I rewrite the introduction as well?
Yes, it is the weakest part. At the moment it begins with a general statement about technology changing society, which tells the reader nothing.
Start with a real dilemma a judge faces.
Like deciding whether to follow a score that disagrees with their own judgement.
Precisely. Send me a new version by the end of the month, and we will meet again in the first week of December.
I will. Thank you, Dr Hale, this has been really useful.

qs.q: What is the supervisor's main criticism of the proposal at the start?
o: It lacks a clear research question.
It combines several projects in one study.
It ignores how fair trials feel to people.
qs.why: ذكرت أنها ثلاثة مشاريع لا مشروع واحد، والنطاق أوسع مما ينبغي.

qs.q: The supervisor refuses to let Samira mention translation software anywhere in the thesis.
qs.why: وافقت على فقرة قصيرة عنها في الخاتمة كاتجاه مستقبلي.

qs.q: Samira thinks she may only manage to interview ___ judges.
qs.why: الأربعون خطتها الأصلية، لكنها قد تصل إلى خمسة عشر فقط.

qs.q: What difficulty does Samira expect with some courts?
o: They will not give interview times.
They will refuse ethics approval.
They will not permit recording.
qs.why: قالت إن بعض المحاكم لا تسمح بالتسجيل فستعتمد على ملاحظات مكتوبة.

qs.q: What does the supervisor advise about the vendor's offer?
o: Insist on a written right to publish the findings.
Reject any cooperation with a company.
Accept it only if the product is praised.
qs.why: نصحت بعقد مكتوب يضمن حق النشر حتى لو كانت النتائج ناقدة.

qs.q: The supervisor says Samira should plan for ___ months of fieldwork.
qs.why: رأت أن ستة أشهر تفاؤل زائد وطلبت تسعة.

qs.q: What does the supervisor say about Samira's reading list?
o: It contains too many old sources.
It has hardly any technical sources.
It needs more law cases.
qs.why: القائمة قوية في القانون وتكاد تخلو من علوم الحاسوب.

qs.q: How does the supervisor want the introduction to begin?
o: With a broad statement about technology.
With a summary of the findings.
With a concrete problem a judge faces.
qs.why: طلبت أن تبدأ بمعضلة حقيقية يواجهها القاضي بدل عبارة عامة.

title: Two researchers disagree about interview data

lines.t: Marcus, I have finished the first pass through the interview transcripts, and I think the picture is clearer than we expected.
Go on. I have only managed to read about half of them, so tell me what you found.
Well, out of the thirty-two interviews, twenty-six people said they stopped contacting the council after a first bad experience. That is the central theme for me.
Hold on. Twenty-six sounds large, but how many of those came from the two districts where we recruited through the community centre?
Fourteen, I think. Why does that matter?
Because people who go to a community centre are often there to complain. We may be hearing from the most frustrated residents, not the typical ones.
I see the point, but the other twelve came from the market stalls and the library, and they said the same thing.
Twelve out of eighteen from those places is still high, I admit. But I would not write that most residents distrust the council.
I would write that most of our participants did.
That is a fair distinction, although I find it rather cautious.
Reviewers will not find it cautious. They will find it correct.
Fine. Let us move on to coding. I have been coding line by line and letting the themes emerge, which gave me nine categories.
Nine is too many. We agreed at the start to use the framework from the pilot, with four categories: access, fairness, speed and respect.
The pilot framework missed something important. Several people talked about not understanding the forms, which fits none of your four.
It fits access, surely. If you cannot understand the form, you cannot reach the service.
Not exactly. Access is about opening hours and distance. This is about language and design.
Then add a fifth category called clarity, and merge your other categories into the framework.
That seems like a reasonable compromise. I would still keep a short list of the minor themes in an appendix.
Fine, as long as they do not appear in the main findings.
Another thing. Four interviews were conducted in Arabic and translated by Leila. Should we ask someone else to check them?
I think so. Not because I doubt her, but because translation changes tone, and our whole analysis is about tone.
She has offered to do the back-translation herself.
That would not be independent. Let us ask the university language centre. It should take them about two weeks.
Agreed. One last point, the quotes. I would like to use the strongest ones in the abstract.
Use one at most. An abstract full of quotations looks like a news article, not a study.
All right, one quote. I will draft the findings section tonight and send it to you tomorrow morning.
Good. And I will finish reading the rest of the transcripts, so that I can argue with you properly.
Please do. I suspect you will find even more people who gave up on the forms.
If I do, that is one more reason for the new clarity category.

qs.q: According to Dana, ___ participants stopped contacting the council after one bad experience.
qs.why: قالت إن ستة وعشرين من اثنين وثلاثين توقفوا عن التواصل.

qs.q: Why does Marcus question the recruitment through the community centre?
o: The centre refused to share names.
The people there may be unusually dissatisfied.
The centre is too far from the council.
qs.why: يرى أن مرتادي المركز قد يكونون الأكثر شكوى لا الأكثر تمثيلا.

qs.q: What do they agree to write in the report?
o: Most residents distrust the council.
The council is trusted in two districts.
Most of the participants distrusted the council.
qs.why: اتفقا على أن الأغلبية بين المشاركين لا بين السكان عموما.

qs.q: How did Dana arrive at nine categories?
o: She coded line by line without a fixed framework.
She added new questions to the pilot.
She combined the four pilot categories.
qs.why: قالت إنها رمّزت سطرا سطرا وتركت المحاور تظهر من تلقاء نفسها.

qs.q: They decide to add a fifth category for difficulty with understanding forms.
qs.why: اقترح ماركوس فئة وضوح خامسة ووافقت دانا على الحل الوسط.

qs.q: Who will check the translated interviews?
o: Leila, using back-translation.
Marcus, after reading the transcripts.
Staff from the university language centre.
qs.why: رفض ماركوس أن تراجعها ليلى بنفسها واقترح مركز اللغات.

qs.q: The language centre should need about ___ weeks for the check.
qs.why: قال ماركوس إن العمل سيستغرق نحو أسبوعين.

qs.q: What does Marcus say about quotations in the abstract?
o: Only a single one should be used.
None should be used.
The strongest three should be used.
qs.why: قال استعمل اقتباسا واحدا على الأكثر.

title: Evaluating sources for a literature review

lines.t: Right, we have six sources on public procurement for the literature review and we need to decide which to keep. Tom, you start with the government report.
I like it because it has the most recent figures, but it was written by the very department that runs the system, so I would treat the numbers carefully.
I agree it is biased, but we could still use it as evidence of what officials claim, as long as we say so.
Good idea. What about the consultant's blog?
It is well written and very persuasive, yet there is no method and no data, and the author sells software to procurement offices.
I would drop it. Though I did notice it links to a study, so we can follow that link and read the original.
Okay, so the blog goes, but the study it cites might stay. Now the article from two thousand and nine.
It is the most cited paper on our list, over four thousand citations I think.
Cited a lot, but it is fifteen years old. Procurement rules in most countries have changed since then, particularly after online bidding became compulsory.
I would keep it for the background section, because it defined the key terms everyone uses. For the main argument, we need newer work.
Fine with me. The preprint, then. It has not been through peer review yet.
But the authors are from a reputable university and the sample is huge, covering nine countries.
I am uneasy about it. The conclusions could change after review. How about we include it but mark it clearly as a preprint?
That is what I would do too. Tom?
I would still be cautious, although I can live with that, provided we do not build a whole section on it.
Agreed. Next is the think tank report, which argues that publishing all contracts reduces corruption.
It reads like a campaign document. Every example supports the same conclusion, and nothing in it is critical of the idea.
I would not throw it out completely. It has a useful table comparing disclosure laws in twelve countries, which we cannot find elsewhere.
Then we use the table and cite the report carefully, without repeating its conclusions.
Good compromise. What about the last one, the case study of the hospital in the north?
It is only one hospital, so we cannot generalise. But the detail is wonderful, because it shows how a bribe actually passes through the paperwork.
Then it works as an illustration, not as proof. I will put it in the discussion.
Let us write that down. Who is doing the summary table?
I can do it by Thursday, if you send me the reference list tonight.
I will send it within the hour. And Tom, could you email Dr Nolan and ask whether a preprint is acceptable in a literature review?
Sure, I will do that straight after this meeting.
Brilliant. Then we only need to agree on a reading order for the group presentation.

qs.q: Why does Tom want to treat the government report's figures carefully?
o: The department that produced it runs the system.
The figures are several years out of date.
The report has no clear method.
qs.why: أشار إلى أن التقرير كتبته الإدارة نفسها التي تشغّل النظام.

qs.q: Tom says the consultant's blog has no data and no ___.
qs.why: قال إنه بلا منهج وبلا بيانات.

qs.q: What do the students decide about the article from two thousand and nine?
o: Remove it because it is old.
Use it as the basis of the main argument.
Keep it for the background section.
qs.why: قررت أن تبقيه للخلفية لأنه عرّف المصطلحات الأساسية.

qs.q: Tom is completely comfortable with using the preprint from the start.
qs.why: بقي حذرا ووافق فقط بشرط ألا يُبنى عليه قسم كامل.

qs.q: The think tank report contains a table comparing disclosure laws in ___ countries.
qs.why: التسعة هي عدد دول ورقة ما قبل التحكيم، والجدول يشمل اثنتي عشرة.

qs.q: How will the group use the hospital case study?
o: As an example, not as proof.
As proof that bribery is common.
As the main source for the conclusion.
qs.why: حالة مستشفى واحد لا تعمَّم، فتصلح للتوضيح فقط.

qs.q: Jess promises to finish the summary table by ___.
qs.why: قالت إنها تنجزه بحلول يوم الخميس.

qs.q: What will Tom do after the meeting?
o: Send the reference list to Jess.
Ask the lecturer about using preprints.
Write the section on the think tank.
qs.why: طُلب منه أن يراسل الدكتور نولان بشأن قبول الورقة قبل التحكيم.

lines.t: Today we are looking at whistleblower protection. Omar, you read the case study. Can you start us off?
Yes. It concerns an accountant in a regional hospital who noticed that invoices for cleaning services were being paid twice.
She reported it internally, and within months her contract was not renewed.
Which is the classic pattern, isn't it? The employee does the right thing and the employer finds another reason to remove them.
That is what we need to examine. Hannah, in your essay you argued that the law should shift the burden of proof. Explain that.
Normally, the worker must prove that the dismissal was connected to the report. That is almost impossible. I argued that the employer should have to prove it was not.
I see the logic, but isn't it unfair to employers? Anyone about to be dismissed for poor performance could simply file a report and claim protection.
That is the standard objection, but the evidence from countries that have tried it suggests such abuse is rare. Most people fear reporting, not exploit it.
Omar, are you convinced?
Partly. I would accept the reversed burden if the report was made in good faith and through an official channel, but not if the employee went straight to the press.
I disagree with that. Official channels are often the very place where the problem is hidden. If a manager is part of the fraud, an internal report just warns him.
That raises the question of external reporting. Most laws set out three tiers: first the employer, then a regulator, then the public. What is the thinking behind that?
To give organisations a chance to fix problems before they become scandals, and to protect people from false accusations in the media.
But the tiers can also delay everything. By the time someone reaches the third tier, the evidence may have disappeared.
Good. Let me add a point from the case study. The accountant had no lawyer, and she could not afford one. Does that matter?
A great deal. Rights that exist on paper are useless if a person cannot afford to use them.
I think free legal advice is more important than any change in the burden of proof.
I would put them on the same level, to be fair. Though I accept that without advice, most people never reach a tribunal.
What about financial rewards? Some systems give whistleblowers a percentage of the money recovered.
I am against that. It changes the motive, and defence lawyers will say the witness is only in it for the money.
I used to think so too, but the sums recovered are huge, and rewards do make people come forward.
I think a small reward is acceptable, as long as the report is checked independently.
We are almost out of time. Let me ask each of you for one recommendation for the hospital's board, in a sentence.
Set up an anonymous reporting line run by someone outside the hospital.
Promise in writing that nobody will be dismissed for six months after reporting, unless the hospital proves a separate reason.
Thank you both. For next week, please read the two statutes on the reading list and bring one example of how each protects a worker.
Will the examples need to come from real cases, or can they be hypothetical?
Real cases, please. They are much easier to discuss.

qs.q: What happened to the accountant in the case study?
o: She was dismissed immediately after reporting.
She was paid twice for her work.
Her contract was not renewed after she reported internally.
qs.why: أبلغت داخليا ثم لم يُجدَّد عقدها بعد أشهر.

qs.q: What does Hannah propose about the burden of proof?
o: The employer should prove the dismissal was unconnected.
The worker should prove the report was honest.
The tribunal should collect the evidence itself.
qs.why: اقترحت أن يُثبت صاحب العمل أن الفصل لا علاقة له بالتبليغ.

qs.q: What is Omar's objection to this idea?
o: Reporting is too costly for workers.
Employees facing dismissal might use reports to protect themselves.
Employers would stop hiring accountants.
qs.why: خشي أن يقدّم من سيُفصل بلاغا ليحتمي به.

qs.q: Hannah says that misuse of such protection is common in countries that have introduced it.
qs.why: قالت إن إساءة الاستعمال نادرة، فالناس يخافون من التبليغ.

qs.q: Why does Hannah reject Omar's condition about official channels?
o: Managers may be involved in the wrongdoing.
The press is more reliable than regulators.
Official channels take too many months.
qs.why: إن كان المدير متورطا فالبلاغ الداخلي ينبّهه فقط.

qs.q: What does Omar consider the most important improvement?
o: A reward for whistleblowers.
A change in the burden of proof.
Free legal advice.
qs.why: رأى أن الاستشارة القانونية المجانية أهم من تغيير عبء الإثبات.

qs.q: What is Hannah's view on financial rewards now?
o: She opposes them completely.
She accepts small ones if the report is verified.
She wants rewards to be as large as possible.
qs.why: غيّرت رأيها وقبلت مكافأة صغيرة بشرط التحقق المستقل.

qs.q: Hannah's recommendation protects staff from dismissal for ___ after reporting.
qs.why: اقترحت وعدا مكتوبا بعدم الفصل لمدة ستة أشهر.

lines.t: Thank you both for making time. I have just presented the pitch, and I would love your honest reaction.
I will start with the positive. The opening story about the bakery owner who lost a contract because he missed a deadline was excellent. I could picture him.
I agree, that was the strongest moment. My concern is what came next. You went straight into twelve slides of technology and the audience lost the thread.
I thought investors wanted to see that the technology is sound.
They do, but later. First they want to know who pays, how much, and why they will not leave.
Which brings me to pricing. You are charging forty pounds a month. For a business with five employees that sounds low, and low prices make people suspicious.
I disagree a little. For a very small business forty pounds is already a stretch. I would keep it but add a higher plan with extra features for larger companies.
We have discussed a premium tier, with automatic bid drafting.
Then put it on the slide. At the moment I only saw it in your notes.
Okay. What about the market size? I said there are two million small firms.
That is the number I would remove. You have not explained which of those firms actually bid for public contracts, and most never will.
Start with the ones that do, even if the number is smaller, perhaps three hundred thousand.
Exactly. A small, believable number beats a huge one that nobody trusts.
Hmm, I worry that three hundred thousand sounds too small to be exciting.
Investors are not looking for excitement at that point. They are looking for a plan to win the first ten thousand customers.
And I only have a hundred and twenty at the moment.
Which is a good start, as long as you say how many of them still pay after three months. Do you know?
Around seventy percent.
That is a strong figure! Put it on the slide next to the bakery story. It proves the story is not an exception.
One more point, about the competition. You said you have none.
Well, nobody does exactly what we do.
Everybody has competitors, even if it is only spreadsheets and email. Name them, and explain why your product is better than a spreadsheet.
I would add a short live demonstration. Two minutes, showing a tender notice becoming a checklist.
I was afraid the internet would fail during the pitch.
Record it as a video, then. That way nothing can go wrong, and you still show the product working.
That makes sense. Should I cut anything to stay within ten minutes?
Yes, the team slide. Keep one sentence about it, because your experience is already clear from the opening.
Right. I will rebuild it this weekend and send a new version on Monday.
Send it to both of us. And practise out loud, because your delivery was a little fast.

qs.q: Which part of the pitch did the mentors like most?
o: The slides about the technology.
The pricing explanation.
The opening story about a small business owner.
qs.why: أشاد كلاهما بقصة صاحب المخبز في البداية.

qs.q: What is Ruth's main criticism of the structure?
o: The technology section came too early and was too long.
The founder spoke for too long about her team.
The ending did not include any figures.
qs.why: انتقلت مباشرة إلى اثنتي عشرة شريحة تقنية فضاع الجمهور.

qs.q: The current subscription costs ___ pounds a month.
qs.why: ذكرت الباحثة أن السعر أربعون جنيها شهريا.

qs.q: What does Ruth suggest about the price?
o: Lower it for very small firms.
Keep it and add a more expensive plan.
Raise it immediately to avoid suspicion.
qs.why: خالفت غريغ واقترحت إبقاء السعر مع خطة أعلى.

qs.q: Greg suggests a starting market of about ___ firms.
qs.why: اقترح ثلاثمئة ألف شركة تشارك فعلا في العقود العمومية.

qs.q: Greg is impressed by the proportion of customers who are still paying after three months.
qs.why: وصف نسبة السبعين بالمئة بأنها رقم قوي.

qs.q: What does Greg recommend instead of a live demonstration online?
o: A printed handout.
A recorded video of the product.
A longer question session.
qs.why: خوفا من انقطاع الإنترنت اقترح تسجيل العرض بالفيديو.

qs.q: What should the founder do with the team slide?
o: Move it to the end.
Add more photographs.
Reduce it to a single sentence.
qs.why: نصحتها روث بجملة واحدة لأن خبرتها واضحة من البداية.
